points.description: States FALSE (the statement is incorrect; processes of the same program do not share a single PCB).
States that each process is an independent entity / has its own separate PCB (separate OS state) even when created from the same executable.

Justifies by naming the per-process state that must be tracked separately: execution state/context, memory contents/allocations, open files, stack state (at least memory, open files and stack/execution state named).
points.partial_credit: Only one or two of these state items named precisely earns no more than half of the marks of this point (give 0.25 if two named).

points.description: Concludes that a shared PCB (with a reference counter) cannot provide this per-process semantics/isolation.

rubric.notes: Full marks need FALSE plus a precise justification: separate PCB per process, per-process state (memory, open files, stack, execution state), and a shared PCB cannot provide this. No correct justification means 0 overall, even if FALSE is stated. Vague statements like 'processes are different' without the PCB/state link earn nothing for that point; any claim that a shared PCB with a reference counter is valid voids the relevant points.
